QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_50

question.text: An exchange-traded index futures contract has a quoted price of 52,400 and a lot size of 30. The current NISM VIII workbook (p.32) states that derivative contract values should be not less than Rs. 15 lakh at introduction and within Rs. 15–20 lakh on review. Computed as Price × Lot Size, what is the contract value, and is it consistent with the current contract-value range?

answer.text: Rs. 7,86,000 — within the current Rs. 15–20 lakh range
Rs. 15,72,000 — within the current Rs. 15–20 lakh range required by SEBI/exchange for derivative contracts at introduction/review
Rs. 78,60,000 — well above the current Rs. 15–20 lakh range
Rs. 3,49,333 — below the current Rs. 15 lakh minimum

explanation.text: The Logic: Contract Value = Price × Lot Size = 52,400 × 30 = Rs. 15,72,000. Per the current NISM VIII workbook (p.32), derivative contract values should be not less than Rs. 15 lakh at introduction and within Rs. 15–20 lakh on review, so Rs. 15.72 lakh sits within that range. The Trap: The legacy Bank Nifty lot size of 15 (giving a contract value of about Rs. 7.86 lakh) falls below the current Rs. 15-lakh minimum. Lot sizes are determined by the exchange and revised periodically; the current source range — not a fixed legacy lot size — is the relevant test. Cross-Exam Context: NISM VIII tests both the contract-value computation and the current SEBI/exchange contract-value range at introduction and review.
